title: Agedashi Tofu Crispy Dashi

description: Agedashi Tofu Crispy Dashi is a beloved Japanese dish featuring delicate tofu lightly fried to a golden crisp. It is served in a warm, savory dashi broth, offering a delightful contrast of textures and flavors. This vegetarian classic is perfect as an appetizer or a light, comforting meal.

instructions.title: Prepare the Tofu
instructions.text: Gently press the block of tofu for at least 20 minutes to remove excess water. Wrap it in paper towels or a clean cloth and place a weighted plate on top. Once pressed, cut the tofu into 8 uniform cubes, about 1.5 inches each.

instructions.title: Make the Vegetarian Dashi Broth
instructions.text: In a small saucepan, combine the vegetarian dashi broth, soy sauce, and mirin. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce heat to low to keep it warm. Do not boil vigorously.

instructions.title: Coat the Tofu
instructions.text: Place the potato starch or cornstarch in a shallow dish. Carefully dredge each tofu cube in the starch, ensuring it is evenly coated on all sides. Gently shake off any excess starch.

instructions.title: Fry the Tofu
instructions.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pot or frying pan to 350F (175C). Carefully add the coated tofu cubes, frying in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Fry for 3-5 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crispy.

instructions.title: Drain and Assemble
instructions.text: Once fried, use a slotted spoon to remove the tofu from the oil and place it on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil. Arrange 2-3 pieces of crispy tofu in individual serving bowls.

instructions.title: Serve with Dashi and Garnish
instructions.text: Ladle the warm dashi broth generously over the tofu in each bowl. Garnish immediately with a spoonful of grated daikon radish and a sprinkle of fresh chopped green onions. For a touch of spice, add a pinch of shichimi togarashi. Serve hot.

tips: For the crispiest tofu, ensure your oil is at the correct temperature (350F/175C) and avoid overcrowding the pan, which can lower the oil temperature and lead to soggy tofu.
If you cannot find daikon radish, a light sprinkle of finely julienned ginger can offer a similar fresh, pungent counterpoint to the rich tofu and dashi.
Agedashi Tofu is best enjoyed immediately after preparation when the tofu is at its crispiest and the dashi is warm. If storing, keep the tofu and dashi separate and reheat gently before combining.
